In `EmbeddableHost` the `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!` twice. If `host` is `nil` (e.g., missing `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`), this will raise `NoMethodError` before the `validates_format_of :host` validation can add an error. The diff does not guard against `nil` (e.g. `return if host.blank?`).

In `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` (around line 17), the query is `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` but `host` is not downcased. If the referer URL has an uppercase hostname (valid in URLs), `lower(host)` will be compared to e.g. `"EvilTrout.com"` and won’t match, incorrectly rejecting an otherwise allowed host. It should pass `host.downcase` (or downcase earlier).

In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` (around line 10) and `#destroy` (around line 15), the record is fetched with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If no record exists, `host` will be `nil`, but `update` then calls `save_host(host)` which immediately dereferences it (`host.host = ...`), and `destroy` calls `host.destroy`. Both would raise a `NoMethodError` instead of returning

The new `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` adds real behavior (`create/update/destroy` and `save_host` param handling/defaulting to `uncategorized_category_id`), but `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` (around line 5) only asserts it subclasses `Admin::AdminController` and does not test any of the controller’s actual actions/logic introduced in this diff.
